summary: Follow-up on the 2027-08-11 production incident where model requests returned 500s and token latency spiked after a serving runtime rollout. We reviewed root cause hypotheses (KV cache invalidation + autoscaler churn), immediate mitigations, longer-term reliability fixes, and next steps for a joint canary and runbook updates.
topics: Root cause hypotheses: KV cache invalidation, autoscaler scaling loops
transcript:
Header: 2027-08-15 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~45 minutes | Attendees: Jordan Lee, Priya Raman, Ethan Wu (Redwood); Aisha Khan, Dr. Mark Renshaw, Luis Ortega, Maya Singh (Cerulean)

00:00:02 Jordan: Alright hi everyone, thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood. We wanted to run through the postmortem follow-up from the 8/11 outage. Quick check, can everyone hear ok?
00:00:10 Aisha: Yep, loud and clear.
00:00:12 Mark: Good.
00:00:15 Jordan: Great. I'll hand over to Priya to summarize the incident briefly, then we'll go into customer timeline and actions.
00:00:22 Priya: Cool, thanks Jordan. So, brief summary — on 2027-08-11 at ~02:14 UTC we saw a sharp increase in 5xx responses from the Redwood endpoint backing Cerulean's clinical routing service. Token latency jumped from median ~120ms to 1.2s, p95 spiked to multi-seconds, and errors reached ~18% of requests for a 16-minute window. We rolled back the serving runtime deploy at 02:33 and errors dropped back.
00:00:49 Ethan: There was also some autoscaler activity around that time — multiple pods repeatedly cycled which likely worsened latencies.
00:00:56 Aisha: Right, from our side we saw downstream consumers timing out and some failed workflow runs. That was painful.
00:01:03 Jordan: Thanks. Mark, do you want to add customer timeline/context?
00:01:06 Mark: Yeah — we had a higher-than-usual batch of requests, some longer prompt lengths for scheduled batch jobs at 02:10. We also had a config change to increase parallelism in our client which might have raised open connections. We pushed that out at 01:58.
00:01:22 Priya: Important context. From Redwood's side the change was a serving runtime optim that changed how KV cache invalidation worked across rollout. The deploy should have been safe but it looks like under the higher concurrency it triggered cache misses and then a feedback loop with the autoscaler.
00:01:40 Luis: Can you explain the KV cache bit — is that the prefix cache? We saw references to 'KV cash' in the alert which confused ops.
00:01:47 Priya: Yeah sorry the transcriber got that — it's KV cache. Essentially the new kernel path changed cache keys on the first few requests after a pod spin up, causing cold misses and higher compute per token. With autoscaler configured conservatively, CPU went high and pods started cycling which increased cold starts.
00:02:06 Jordan: And that created higher latency which caused client timeouts which caused retries and more load — typical spiral.
00:02:12 Aisha: We ran the request traces, you can see the retry storms from our end. We'll upload them.
00:02:18 Jordan: Perfect, thanks. Ok next — mitigations we did during the incident. Priya?
00:02:21 Priya: Immediate mitigation was rollback to previous runtime at 02:33, which restored steady-state. We also temporarily increased pod limits and adjusted autoscaler CPU targets to prevent immediate churn. For the longer-term, we recommend a couple of things: one, ensure KV cache compatibility testing in rollout matrix; two, a pre-warm canary phase where the canary receives a low percentage of real traffic and runs under a synthetic load generator; three, improve our dashboard alerts to correlate cache miss rate, pod churn, and client retry counts.
00:02:54 Ethan: We also want to add a circuit-breaker on the client side — short-term config you can flip to reduce retries.
00:03:00 Mark: How intrusive is the pre-warm canary? If it requires significant infra changes that's a blocker for us.
00:03:07 Priya: It should be minimal. Canary is a deploy policy plus a small synthetic load job that runs for 5-10 minutes. We can provide the automation snippet. Ethan will own that.
00:03:17 Ethan: Yep I'll share the Jenkins/GHA snippet and the checklist.
00:03:20 Aisha: Ok good. On observability — we need more granular traces. Right now our logs show errors but don't tie to request ids across the chain.
00:03:29 Priya: Agreed. We're adding a request-id propagation check and will expose a trace link in the Redwood console for any 5xx. We'll also add a 'KV miss rate' metric and a tagging field for kernel path version.
00:03:42 Maya: From compliance perspective, we need to capture the audit trail for that deploy and the rollback — evidence for SOC 2 audit. Can Redwood export those artifacts?
00:03:50 Jordan: Yes, we have audit logs and the deploy artifact IDs. We'll share the deploy timeline and logs as part of the postmortem package.
00:03:57 Maya: Also need encryption key access logs — were any KMS rotations happening?
00:04:01 Priya: No key rotations at that time. KMS logs show no activity during the window; we'll attach that.
00:04:07 Aisha: One thing we noticed — client-level timeouts were 3s causing retries to pile up. Would lowering client retries have prevented the spiral?
00:04:14 Priya: Likely yes. We recommend reducing retries to 1 for high-latency windows and using exponential backoff with jitter. Again, we can provide client config.
00:04:24 Mark: For longer-term — you mentioned autoscaler tuning. Can we get a set of recommended autoscaler parameters for our traffic profile?
00:04:30 Ethan: Yes, we have tuned profiles: bursty batch jobs vs steady low-latency. We'll recommend target CPU, stabilization windows, and max surge to avoid thrash.
00:04:40 Jordan: I'll include those in the runbook doc.
00:04:43 Aisha: Great. Any other root cause candidates?
00:04:46 Priya: We considered GC pauses and kernel scheduler differences, but traces point strongly to cache behavior combined with concurrency. There's a secondary vector where the autoscaler reacts to ephemeral CPU spikes and creates churn.
00:04:59 Luis: Ok makes sense.
00:05:01 Jordan: Let's walk through the proposed timeline of actions and owners — then recap and next steps.
00:05:06 Priya: For short-term: (1) Redwood to add KV cache metric and kernel-tagging to prod dashboards — ETA 2027-08-18; (2) Shared runbook update with canary checklist and client circuit-breaker snippet — ETA 2027-08-18; (3) Priya to run a KV cache stress test in staging to reproduce and share artifacts — ETA 2027-08-20.
00:05:28 Ethan: (4) I'll prepare canary automation and a sample synthetic load job — ETA 2027-08-19.
00:05:33 Aisha: From Cerulean: we'll export traces and traffic samples for 08-11 and share by 2027-08-17. We'll also temporarily drop client retries as a config change and test in pre-prod.
00:05:44 Maya: We'll confirm the compliance scope if we consider private deployment — not decided yet — but will get back by 2027-08-25.
00:05:51 Jordan: Sounds good. Any concerns about the rollback safety? We want to avoid repeated rollbacks in production.
00:05:57 Priya: Rollback is safe but disruptive. The goal is to catch issues in canary/pre-warm to avoid needing rollback. Also we plan to improve the deploy gating so kernel-path or cache-key changes are flagged in preflight tests.
00:06:10 Luis: Will the improved dashboard be available in the console or do we need to add custom metrics to our monitoring?
00:06:14 Priya: We'll surface it in the Redwood console and push a Grafana dashboard snippet you can import into your monitoring.
00:06:20 Mark: Good. What about SLA credit or incident review with finance? We had downstream outages affecting customers — is there escalation for any commercial remedies?
00:06:28 Jordan: We have the incident review and can open a support ticket about credits; I'll coordinate with customer success and your account team after this call.
00:06:35 Mark: Thanks.
00:06:36 Aisha: One small note — the alert thresholds didn't trigger early enough. We had an alert at 02:18 but not at 02:12 when latency ramped. Can you adjust alert sensitivity?
00:06:45 Priya: We'll add an early-warning alert correlated across KV misses, CPU, and retries. We'll test the alert logic in staging before changing prod thresholds.
00:06:55 Jordan: Ok wrapping up — quick recap: Redwood to share postmortem doc + dashboards + runbook updates by 8/18; Cerulean to send traces by 8/17; Priya to run KV stress test by 8/20; canary test planned for week of 8/22. We'll schedule a 30-min follow-up 48 hours after the canary test to review. Any last questions?
00:07:20 Mark: No, that's clear. Thanks everyone.
00:07:23 Aisha: Thanks.
00:07:25 Jordan: Great, meeting adjourned. We'll send notes and links right after.

Notes/refs: postmortem doc link: https://redwood.example.com/postmortems/cerulean-2027-08-11, dashboard link: https://console.redwood.example.com/orgs/cerulean/dashboards/incident-2027-08-11, ticket: JIRA-CH-5472.

(Transcription notes: occasional word swaps — 'KV cash' -> 'KV cache'; speaker overlap in a few places; timestamps are approximate every 10-60 seconds.)
